name: Evidence for neutrino emission from NGC 1068

significance.quote: We found an excess of $79_{-20}^{+22}$ neutrinos associated with the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068 at a significance of 4.2$\,\sigma$.

summary.plain: IceCube found an excess of about 79 neutrinos associated with the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068, at a significance of 4.2σ. The collaboration interprets it as direct evidence of TeV neutrino emission from a nearby active galaxy, and says the inferred neutrino flux exceeds the potential TeV gamma-ray flux by at least one order of magnitude.
summary.technical: Point-source search over 2011–2020 data with improved reconstruction and calibration; 110 a priori selected gamma-ray sources analysed individually. An excess of 79 (+22/−20) neutrinos associated with NGC 1068 at a significance of 4.2σ, spatially consistent with the direction of the strongest clustering of neutrinos in the Northern Sky and interpreted as direct evidence of TeV neutrino emission from a nearby active galaxy; the inferred flux exceeds the potential TeV gamma-ray flux by at least one order of magnitude.

title: Evidence for neutrino emission from the nearby active galaxy NGC 1068
why_it_matters: The abstract interprets the excess, spatially consistent with the direction of the strongest clustering of neutrinos in the Northern Sky, as direct evidence of TeV neutrino emission from a nearby active galaxy.
